1. The petitioner is before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C. No.3302/2021 registered for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act,
(hereinafter referred to as the "Act" for short).
2. Heard the learned counsel Sri.Aravind D. Kulkarni appearing for the petitioner.
3. The petitioner is the accused, the respondent - complainant.

The accused and the complainant appear to have had a transaction and in furtherance of the said transaction, it is the claim of the complainant that a particular cheque was issued by the petitioner - accused.
The cheque was presented for its realization on 13.01.2020.
It is returned on 17.01.2020 with an indication of "Payment Stopped By Drawer".
Therefore, the complainant seeks to register a complaint invoking Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. for offence punishable under Section 138 of the Act on 20.02.2020.

The concerned Court takes cognizance of the offence and issues summons to the NC:
2023:KHC-D:10818 petitioner.
Taking of cognizance and issuance of summons to the petitioner is what drives the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner Sri.Aravind D. Kulkarni would take this Court through the documents appended to the petition, as also a memo alongwith other documents, to demonstrate that long before the cheque was presented, the petitioner had registered a crime against the complainant for the offence of thieving under Section 379 of the IPC alongwith Sections 420 and 468 of the IPC for forging the cheque.
The Police after investigation have filed a charge sheet in the matter on 09.04.2023.
It is in the interregnum, the complainant registers the complaint before the learned Magistrate after having presented the cheque.
It is therefore, he submits that the cheque is stolen and there is prima facie evidence for it having been stolen.
The petitioner has not issued any cheque to the complainant.
The complainant though served long ago remains unrepresented.
Therefore, the petitioner is heard in the matter.

6. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective counsel and Ayubkha Azizakhan Pathan vs Ashok S/O Ratnavva Marennvar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47254703/

sentences.text: 7. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
It is the case of the complainant that the petitioner had issued a cheque for an amount of Rs.5,00,000/-.
Rs.5,00,000/- is said to have been borrowed by the petitioner as a hand loan.
In furtherance of the said hand loan, the cheque is allegedly issued.
The cheque is presented on 13.01.2020.
Four months prior to the said date, i.e., on 16.09.2019, the petitioner had registered a complaint before the jurisdictional Police on the allegation that documents are lost.
This was not taken into consideration and a non- cognizable report was issued on 16.09.2019.

The petitioner then pursued the remedy of filing a private complaint before the learned Magistrate and pursuant to the reference made by the learned Magistrate under NC:
2023:KHC-D:10818 Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C., the Police conduct investigation and have filed a charge sheet against the complainant for the offences punishable under Sections 379, 403, 420, 468 and 469 of the IPC.
The offences alleged are Sections 379, 403, 420, 468 and 469 of the IPC.
The crux of the complaint is stealing of the cheque book.
The cheque leaf that is presented to the Bank is one of those leaves that form the stolen cheque book.

This is the finding by the Police after investigation, as obtaining in column No.17 of Crime No.62/20222 which is now pending as C.C.
No.62/2023.
8.

In the light of the said fact of the Police filing a charge sheet prima facie case is made out by the petitioner to demonstrate that the cheque that was presented before the Bank by the respondent - complainant was a cheque that was stolen and then presented.

The contention stands to reason as there is no document produced to demonstrate that there was a hand loan taken by the petitioner for Rs.5,00,000/-, in exchange of which the petitioner had issued the cheque.

NC: 2023:KHC-D:10818 The charge sheet being filed against the complainant would enure to the benefit of the petitioner leading to obliteration of the proceedings pending before the concerned Court for offence punishable under Section 138 of the Act.
9.

For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
( ii )
The proceedings and the complaint in C.C. No.3302/2021 on the file of the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Haveri stands quashed.
